cards.title: Voltage Drop Signals Wiring Problems
cards.body: High resistance in long wire runs drops voltage before it reaches field sensors. Loose wire terminals or corrosion often cause unexpected voltage drops. Checking voltage under load helps spot hidden connection problems before sensors fail.

cards.title: Zero and Span Calibrate Field Devices
cards.body: Calibrating a field sensor requires setting both its zero and span points. Zero adjusts the lower end of the measurement range, while span sets the upper limit. Adjusting one setting can shift the other, so technicians always recheck both points.

cards.title: Temperature Sensors Suffer from Thermal Lag
cards.body: Temperature sensors take time to respond to rapid temperature shifts in wind turbine gearboxes. Thermowells protect sensors from direct fluid pressure but slow down measurement response times. Allow the process temperature to stabilize before recording calibration points.

cards.title: Four Milliamps Signals Live Zero
cards.body: Current loops use four milliamperes to represent zero process value instead of zero milliamperes. A reading of zero milliamperes instantly indicates a broken wire or power loss rather than a low reading. This live zero design helps system controllers detect damaged cables immediately.

cards.title: Termination Resistors Stop Data Reflections
cards.body: Serial Modbus networks rely on resistor terminations at both physical ends of the cable run. Missing or extra termination resistors cause signal reflections that corrupt data packets. Measuring total line resistance with power off reveals improper termination setups.

cards.title: Tag Numbers Locate Physical Field Instruments
cards.body: Piping and instrumentation diagrams use standard letter codes for what an instrument does. A tag starting with PT is a pressure transmitter, and TT is a temperature transmitter. The number after the letters is the loop number, which ties the instrument to its control loop and its datasheet.

cards.title: Stored Energy Remains After Power Off
cards.body: Disconnecting main electrical breakers does not remove all hazards from process equipment. Hydraulic accumulators, charged capacitors, and mechanical tension retain dangerous energy after power shutoff. Technicians must bleed pressure and discharge components before starting maintenance work.

cards.title: Full Harness Inspection Prevents Equipment Failure
cards.body: Technicians climbing wind turbine towers must inspect fall protection gear before every ascent. Webbing cuts, chemical damage, or bent D-rings compromise safety under shock loads. Connecting to approved anchorage points ensures fall arrest systems function during an emergency.

cards.title: Ladder Logic Reads Inputs Before Outputs
cards.body: Programmable logic controllers continuously scan inputs, run control logic, and update outputs. Rungs in ladder logic execute sequentially from top to bottom and left to right. Understanding this scan cycle helps explain why output changes lag input signals by a fraction of a second.

cards.title: Trend Graphs Reveal Impending Bearing Wear
cards.body: SCADA software plots vibration and temperature data over time to show equipment health. A gradual upward trend in vibration usually points to mechanical bearing wear long before alarms trigger. Catching these subtle patterns early prevents catastrophic gear failure in wind turbines.
